correctness.rationale: Fourier-transform the actual left action in x and z. For each pair of characters (k,l), the n-dimensional y-space has X diagonal with entries zeta^(k+l*y), and Y a unit cyclic shift. For m the order of zeta^l, Y^m commutes with both and has all (n/m)-th roots as eigenvalues, each on an m-dimensional block. X^m is zeta^(km), with each permitted scalar occurring for m values of k. There are phi(m) choices of l. On each block, the identity and full cyclic shift give the determinant, with sign positive because m is odd; the m=1 block is just scalar. If the shift coefficient is nonzero, the cyclic first-order kernel recurrence takes a solution from a single initial coordinate. If that coefficient is zero and the diagonal generator has nonzero coefficient, distinct diagonal entries imply at most one zero; scalar-only and all-zero operators are covered separately. Hence the displayed singular factors count actual dimensions, not determinant multiplicities alone. In the unweighted case the only cancelling ordered pairs are the two primitive cube roots in either order, and multiplicativity of the resulting divisor sum gives the claimed product.
